statement: To find two straight lines incommensurable in square which make the sum of the squares on them medial but the rectangle contained by them rational.
heath_proof: Let there be set out two medial straight lines AB, BC, commensurable in square only, such that the rectangle which they contain is rational, and the square on AB is greater than the square on BC by the square on a straight line incommensurable with AB; [X. 31, ad fin.]let the semicircle ADB be described on AB, let BC be bisected at E, let there be applied to AB a parallelogram equal to the square on BE and deficient by a square figure, namely the rectangle AF, FB; [VI. 28] therefore AF is incommensurable in length with FB. [X. 18] Let FD be drawn from F at right angles to AB, and let AD, DB be joined. Since AF is incommensurable in length with FB, therefore the rectangle BA, AF is also incommensurable with the rectangle AB, BF. [X. 11] But the rectangle BA, AF is equal to the square on AD, and the rectangle AB, BF to the square on DB; therefore the square on AD is also incommensurable with the square on DB. And, since the square on AB is medial, therefore the sum of the squares on AD, DB is also medial. [III. 31, I. 47] And, since BC is double of DF, therefore the rectangle AB, BC is also double of the rectangle AB, FD. But the rectangle AB, BC is rational; therefore the rectangle AB, FD is also rational. [X. 6] But the rectangle AB, FD is equal to the rectangle AD, DB; [Lemma]so that the rectangle AD, DB is also rational. Therefore two straight lines AD, DB incommensurable in square have been found which make the sum of the squares on them medial, but the rectangle contained by them rational.
ai_proof_text:
10.34
**Statement:** To find two straight lines incommensurable in square which make the sum of the squares on them medial but the rectangle contained by them rational.

Notation: sq(X) denotes the square on X; rect(X, Y) the rectangle contained by X and Y.

**Step 1.** By 10.31, taken in the form noted at its close (its construction carried out from the two rational straight lines commensurable in square only furnished by 10.30 in place of those of 10.29), set out two medial straight lines AB, BC commensurable in square only, containing a rational rectangle rect(AB, BC), AB being the greater, and such that sq(AB) is greater than sq(BC) by the square on a straight line incommensurable in length with AB.

**Step 2.** Bisect AB at G and BC at E (1.10). With centre G and distance GA describe a circle (P3), and let ADB be the semicircle on AB lying on one side of it. Since BC is less than AB, its half BE is less than GB, the half of AB, so sq(BE) is not greater than sq(GB), the square described on the half of AB; hence by 6.28 a parallelogram equal to sq(BE) and deficient by a square figure can be applied to AB. Let it be rect(AF, FB), F lying on AB, so that rect(AF, FB) = sq(BE).

**Step 3.** Since BC is double BE, sq(BC) is four times sq(BE); thus rect(AF, FB), which equals sq(BE), is the fourth part of sq(BC), and it has been applied to the greater line AB deficient by a square figure. Since sq(AB) exceeds sq(BC) by the square on a straight line incommensurable with AB (Step 1), 10.18 shows that AF is incommensurable in length with FB.

**Step 4.** From the point F draw FD at right angles to AB (1.11), meeting the semicircle at D, and join AD, DB (P1). Since ADB is an angle in a semicircle, the angle ADB is right (3.31). Thus in the right-angled triangle ADB the perpendicular DF has been drawn from the right angle to the base AB; therefore the triangles ADF, DBF are each similar to the whole triangle ADB and to one another (6.8).

**Step 5.** Since triangle ABD is equiangular with triangle ADF, BA : AD = AD : AF (6.4); therefore sq(AD) = rect(BA, AF) (6.17). Since triangle ABD is equiangular with triangle DBF, AB : BD = BD : BF (6.4); therefore sq(DB) = rect(AB, BF) (6.17). Since triangle ADF is equiangular with triangle DBF, AF : DF = DF : FB (6.4); therefore sq(DF) = rect(AF, FB) (6.17).

**Step 6.** The rectangles rect(BA, AF) and rect(AB, BF) have the same height AB, so rect(BA, AF) : rect(AB, BF) = AF : FB (6.1). Since AF is incommensurable in length with FB (Step 3), rect(BA, AF) is incommensurable with rect(AB, BF) (10.11). By Step 5 these rectangles are equal to sq(AD) and sq(DB) respectively; therefore sq(AD) is incommensurable with sq(DB), that is, AD and DB are incommensurable in square (D10.1.2).

**Step 7.** Since the angle ADB is right, sq(AD) + sq(DB) = sq(AB) (1.47). But AB is a medial straight line, so the square on it is a medial area (10.21). Therefore the sum of the squares on AD, DB is medial.

**Step 8.** By Step 5, sq(DF) = rect(AF, FB), and by Step 2, rect(AF, FB) = sq(BE); therefore sq(DF) = sq(BE) (CN1), and consequently DF = BE. Since BC is double BE, BC is double DF.

**Step 9.** The rectangles rect(AB, BC) and rect(AB, DF) have the same height AB, so rect(AB, BC) : rect(AB, DF) = BC : DF (6.1), which is the ratio 2 : 1, the ratio which a number has to a number; therefore rect(AB, BC) is commensurable with rect(AB, DF) (10.6). But rect(AB, BC) is rational (Step 1), that is, commensurable with the square on the assigned rational straight line (D10.1.4); hence rect(AB, DF), being commensurable with rect(AB, BC), is commensurable with that same square (10.12), and is therefore rational (D10.1.4).

**Step 10.** The rectangle contained by AD, DB is a parallelogram having the same base DB as the triangle ADB and lying in the same parallels, because its side AD is at right angles to DB; hence rect(AD, DB) is double the triangle ADB (1.41). Again, the rectangle contained by AB, DF is a parallelogram on the base AB lying in the same parallels as the triangle ADB, because DF is the perpendicular from D to AB; hence rect(AB, DF) is also double the triangle ADB (1.41). Therefore rect(AD, DB) = rect(AB, DF) (CN1), and by Step 9 rect(AD, DB) is rational.

**Step 11.** Therefore AD, DB are two straight lines incommensurable in square (Step 6) which make the sum of the squares on them medial (Step 7) but the rectangle contained by them rational (Step 10). Q.E.F.

Path note: the equality rect(AD, DB) = rect(AB, DF) in Step 10 could equally be obtained from the similar triangles ABD, DBF of Step 4 (AB : BD = AD : DF, whence the rectangles are equal by 6.16); the area route through 1.41 was chosen as the more direct.
